GPU-accelerated rendering with adaptive sampling that prioritizes detail where it matters. Redshift is a GPU-accelerated 3D rendering software from Maxon that turns 3D scenes into production-quality images and animations. Redshift combines fast, interactive feedback with deep artist control over lighting, materials, and optimization, and runs natively in Cinema 4D and as a plugin for major 3D applications.

Artists and studios use Redshift for motion design, film and episodic VFX, architectural visualization, product imagery, and game cinematics. In other words, anywhere 3D scenes need to become high-quality final frames on a deadline.
Redshift is built into Cinema 4D and offers plugins for Maya, 3ds Max, Houdini, Katana, ZBrush, Vectorworks, and Revit. One subscription includes all integration plugins.
Yes. Every Cinema 4D subscription includes a full version of Redshift, so you can move from scene to final render without extra licensing.

Redshift runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS, with GPU acceleration on NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple M-series hardware. You can also render on the CPU on most systems, including Windows on Arm machines such as Qualcomm X Elite. Check the system requirements page for the current list.
Redshift is optimized for artist control at production speed. You choose how render time is spent, and results stay consistent across machines and teams. For details, see the features page.

Redshift's interactive preview rendering gives immediate visual feedback, which makes learning lighting and materials faster. Inside Cinema 4D, hundreds of real-world material presets let you apply realistic materials to any object straight away. Cineversity training is included with every subscription, and the defaults produce clean results before you ever touch an advanced setting.
